mainTopic: The end of פרק בית שמאי (כופין like רב), then פרק חרש. It covers the marriage, divorce and יבום of a חרש or חרשת, and why the רבנן enacted marriage for them but not for a שוטה or קטן.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a discussion about a woman who made a נדר against her husband's brother. The גמרא first suggests that the משנה is about a woman who has children. It then rejects that idea and concludes that בית דין forces the brother to do חליצה either way, like רב, and פרק בית שמאי closes with the Hadran. A new פרק begins with a משנה about a חרש or חרשת. They can marry and divorce through gestures, and the rule changes when one spouse loses capacity after the wedding. רבי יוחנן בן נורי asks why a wife who became a חרשת can be divorced but a husband who became a חרש cannot. The חכמים answer that a man divorces only by his own will, while a woman can be divorced even against hers. The משנה then works through many cases of two brothers, some deaf and some competent, married to sisters or to unrelated women, and rules on יבום, חליצה and divorce in each. In the גמרא, רמי בר חמא asks why the רבנן set up marriage for a חרש but not for a שוטה or a קטן, and the גמרא explains each difference, including the case of a קטנה. It then begins to ask why a קטנה can do מיאון but a חרשת cannot, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה should have said 'we ask', not 'we force'
steps.stepSummary: The challenge ends: if the woman may have planned to avoid ייבום, the משנה should say בית דין only asks the יבם to do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have said 'we ask him'!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a challenge that started before this section. It argues that the משנה's word 'we force' (כופין) seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenger reads a woman who vows against her יבם as someone who may have planned to dodge ייבום. If she created the problem on purpose, בית דין would not force the brother. It would only ask him, so the משנה should have said מבקשין.

keyTerms.meaning: We ask (בית דין requests, but does not force)
It should have said
We force (בית דין compels him)
The ceremony that frees a widow from ייבום

phrases.english: It should have said 'we ask'!
phrases.notes: The משנה said 'we force'; the question is that it should have said 'we ask'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְבַקְּשִׁין מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge begun in the previous part of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling of כופין for a נדר made during the husband's lifetime.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the woman is suspected of planning to avoid ייבום, the right ruling would be only asking (מבקשין), not forcing.

steps.title: The משנה is about a woman who has children
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the משנה is about a woman who had children, so she never pictured herself facing ייבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A woman who has children. She never thought that far ahead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It narrows the משנה to a woman who had children when she made the נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman with children would only face ייבום if all her children died and then her husband died too. That is too far-fetched for her to have planned around. So her נדר was not a trick, and בית דין can force the brother.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that narrows the case)
Children
It did not enter her mind

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
A woman who has children,
so she did not think that far ahead.
phrases.notes: Literally 'all this did not go up into her mind'. All this means her children dying, then her husband, and then needing ייבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by limiting the משנה to a narrower case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman in the משנה may have planned to avoid ייבום, so 'we force' looks wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since she has children, she had no such plan in mind, so forcing him makes sense.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have spelled out the children difference
steps.stepSummary: If a woman without children only gets 'we ask', the משנה should have taught that difference inside this very case instead of bringing a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if she has no children, what is the law, that we only ask him? If so, the משנה teaches 'If she meant to do this, even during her husband's lifetime we ask him to do חליצה.' Instead of that, it should have drawn the line within this case itself: 'When is this said? When she has children. But if she has no children, we only ask.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 2. If having children really made the difference, the משנה would have said so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does teach a case where בית דין only asks: when she openly meant to avoid ייבום. But the obvious difference to teach, if step 2 were right, would be 'with children we force, without children we ask.' Since the משנה never mentions children, the children answer looks unlikely.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of teaching
She intended this (to avoid ייבום)
Let it draw the line and teach it within this case itself
When is this said? (introduces a limit on a rule)

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין לָהּ בָּנִים, מַאי — מְבַקְּשִׁין?
phrases.english: But if she has no children, what? We ask?
Instead of teaching: 'If she intended this,'
phrases.notes: This quotes the end of our משנה, where she openly meant to block ייבום.

phrases.english: even during her husband's lifetime,
we ask him to do חליצה for her',
let it draw the line and teach it within this case:
When is this said?
When she has children,
but if she has no children, we ask!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵין לָהּ בָּנִים מַאי מְבַקְּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and knocks down the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה is about a woman with children.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If children made the difference, the משנה would have taught the 'without children' case within this same ruling, not a different case.

steps.title: Children or not, בית דין forces him, like רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that having children makes no difference: בית דין forces the יבם either way, which proves רב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: it makes no difference whether she has children or not. We force him, like רב. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the children answer failed, the גמרא concludes that the משנה forces him in every case. That matches רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman is not assumed to have planned to dodge ייבום unless she clearly showed it. So a plain נדר made during her husband's life always leads to כופין, with or without children. The final 'שמע מינה' confirms that the משנה supports רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a proof is accepted)
It makes no difference
Like the view of רב

steps.whatToRemember: A woman who vows against her יבם during her husband's lifetime is not assumed to have planned it. בית דין forces him to do חליצה, children or not, like רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the rule that we do not assume a hidden plan behind a woman's נדר. Only a clear intention to avoid ייבום lowers the ruling to 'we ask'.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
it makes no difference whether she has children
or she has no children,
we force him, like רב.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once step 3 knocks down the children answer, this step draws the final conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בית דין forces the יבם to do חליצה whether or not she has children, like רב.

steps.title: Hadran: closing the chapter בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the formula said at the end of every chapter. It marks the close of פרק בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It adds no new law. It shows that the discussion above was the last one in this chapter, and a new משנה and topic come next.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, בית שמאי

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter after the final conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק בית שמאי is finished.

steps.title: A deaf-mute's marriage and divorce work by gestures
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens: a חרש married to a פקחת, or a פקח married to a חרשת, may divorce or stay married. Marriage and divorce are both done through gestures.
steps.simpleTranslation: A deaf-mute man who married a competent woman, or a competent man who married a deaf-mute woman: if he wants to divorce her, he may; if he wants to stay married, he may. Just as he marries her through gestures, he divorces her through gestures.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It teaches that when one spouse is a חרש or חרשת, the marriage can continue or end, just like any other marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש cannot speak, so he cannot make a regular spoken act of marriage. The משנה says gestures are enough for him to marry. The same gestures are also enough for him to divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute man / woman, who is not treated as fully legally competent
A man / woman with full hearing, speech and understanding
To divorce (literally, to send out)
To keep the marriage going
Through hints or gestures

phrases.english: A deaf-mute man who married a competent woman
and a competent man who married a deaf-mute woman,
if he wants to divorce her, he may divorce her,
and if he wants to keep her as his wife, he may keep her.
Just as he marries through gestures,
so too he divorces through gestures.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֵרֵשׁ שֶׁנָּשָׂא פִּקַּחַת וּפִקֵּחַ שֶׁנָּשָׂא חֵרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק (פרק חרש) right after the closing line of פרק בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When either spouse is a חרש, the husband may divorce or stay married. Divorce is done by gestures, just as the marriage was.

steps.title: When the wife or husband loses capacity after the marriage
steps.stepSummary: If a healthy wife becomes a חרשת, her husband may divorce her or stay married. If she becomes a שוטה, he may not divorce her. If the husband becomes a חרש or שוטה, he can never divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A competent man married a competent woman, and she became a deaf-mute: if he wants, he may divorce her; if he wants, he may keep her. If she became mentally incompetent, he may not divorce her. If he became a deaf-mute or mentally incompetent, he can never divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now looks at a couple who were both healthy at the wedding, and one of them lost capacity later. It gives a different rule depending on who changed and how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife who became a חרשת can still be divorced. A wife who became a שוטה cannot be divorced. A husband who became a חרש or שוטה cannot give a גט at all. The next steps explain why a change in the husband blocks divorce but the wife becoming a חרשת does not.

keyTerms.meaning: She became a deaf-mute
She became mentally incompetent (a שוטה)
Ever / permanently

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא יוציא' for the wife who became a שוטה does not mean the marriage is locked forever by some punishment. It means a גט given to her now would not work.

phrases.english: A competent man who married a competent woman, and she became a deaf-mute,
if he wants, he may divorce her,
and if he wants, he may keep her.
If she became mentally incompetent, he may not divorce her.
If he became a deaf-mute or mentally incompetent,
he can never divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: פִּקֵּחַ שֶׁנָּשָׂא פִּקַּחַת וְנִתְחָרְשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a couple where one spouse was a חרש from the start to a couple where one spouse lost capacity after the wedding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the wife became a חרשת, she may be divorced. If she became a שוטה, she may not be divorced. If the husband became a חרש or שוטה, he can never divorce.

steps.title: Why is the deaf wife different from the deaf husband?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי challenges the unequal rule: why can a wife who became a חרשת be divorced, while a husband who became a חרש cannot divorce?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: Why is it that a woman who became a deaf-mute can be divorced, but a man who became a deaf-mute cannot divorce?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי pushes back on the משנה's rule. He asks why becoming a חרש blocks divorce for the man but not for the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He assumes it is the same condition on both sides, so it should have the same result. If a חרש husband's divorce is no good, then divorcing a חרשת wife should be no good either.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who questions the difference
For what reason? Why?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
For what reason does a woman who became a deaf-mute get divorced,
but a man who became a deaf-mute cannot divorce?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנִּתְחָרְשָׁה יוֹצְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the difference set up in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a wife who became a חרשת can be divorced but a husband who became a חרש cannot divorce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being a חרש is the same condition for either spouse, so the law should be the same for both.

steps.title: A man divorces only willingly, a woman even unwillingly
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the cases are not alike. A woman can be divorced with or without her consent, so her understanding is not needed. A man divorces only by his own will, and a חרש lacks a legally valid will.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: The man who divorces is not like the woman who is divorced. A woman is divorced whether she wants it or not, but a man divorces only when he wants to.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי יוחנן בן נורי's question. They show that the husband and wife play different roles in a divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Divorce depends on what the husband intends, not on what the wife intends. So when the wife lacks capacity, it doesn't stop the גט. When the husband lacks capacity, there is no valid intention behind the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not similar
The one who divorces / the one who is divorced
Willingly and unwillingly

steps.whatToRemember: In a divorce the husband's will is what counts. The wife may be divorced even against her will. That is why the wife becoming a חרשת doesn't block the גט, but the husband becoming a חרש does.

phrases.english: They said to him:
The man who divorces is not similar
to the woman who is divorced,
since the woman is divorced whether she wants it or not,
but the man divorces only when he wants to.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הָאִישׁ הַמְגָרֵשׁ לָאִשָּׁה הַמִּתְגָּרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן בן נורי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the roles: the husband is the active divorcer and the wife is the passive recipient.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Becoming a חרש should affect the man and the woman the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the husband's will is required for a divorce, so only his lack of capacity blocks it.

steps.title: Testimony: a deaf girl married off by her father can be divorced
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testifies that a חרשת whose father married her off can be divorced with a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testified about a deaf-mute girl whose father married her off, that she can be divorced with a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: A new voice brings a testimony, an accepted tradition, about a related case. It sets up the חכמים's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her father married her off, so her marriage is a full marriage even though she is a חרשת. Even so, she can be divorced with a גט despite her lack of capacity.

keyTerms.meaning: Testified (gave an accepted tradition)
A תנא known for his testimonies
Whose father married her off
Bill of divorce

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgada testified
about a deaf-mute girl whose father married her off,
that she is divorced with a גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related tradition: a woman without capacity who can still receive a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חרשת married off by her father can be divorced with a גט.

steps.title: The חכמים: the wife who became deaf is the same
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים respond that the woman who became a חרשת after marriage is just like the girl in the testimony. She too can receive a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: This woman too is similar to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים link the testimony back to the משנה's case of a wife who became a חרשת. They treat the two cases as the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The girl in the testimony shows that a woman without capacity can still be divorced with a גט. So the earlier rule, that a wife who became a חרשת may be divorced, is backed by this accepted tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too
Like her / similar to her

steps.whatToRemember: A woman's lack of capacity does not stop her from receiving a גט. A husband's lack of capacity does stop him from giving one.

phrases.english: They said to him:
This woman too is similar to her.
phrases.notes: 'This woman' is the healthy wife who became a חרשת after the wedding, from earlier in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַף זוֹ כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא's testimony to the משנה's case.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a wife who became a חרשת can be divorced.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא's testimony that a חרשת married off by her father is divorced with a גט.

steps.title: Two brothers married to two sisters with deaf-mutes involved: exempt from both
steps.stepSummary: In every listed mix of deaf and competent brothers married to sisters, the widow is exempt from חליצה and יבום. If the women were not sisters, the brothers do יבום and may later divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two deaf brothers married to two deaf sisters, or to two competent sisters, or to one deaf and one competent sister. Or two deaf sisters married to two competent brothers, or to two deaf brothers, or to one deaf and one competent brother. In all these cases the widow is exempt from חליצה and from יבום. If the women were unrelated, the brothers marry them, and if they want to divorce, they may divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new topic: יבום cases where the couples include חרשים and the two wives are sisters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case, when one brother dies, his widow is the sister of the surviving brother's wife, so she is forbidden to him as אחות אשה. That frees her from both יבום and חליצה. If the wives are not sisters, that problem disappears, and the brother marries her through יבום. Afterward he may divorce her like any wife.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
Marriage of a childless man's widow to his brother
A legally competent man or woman
Unrelated women, here meaning wives who are not sisters to each other
Wife's sister, a forbidden relative

steps.confusionAlert: נכריות here does not mean non-Jewish women. It just means the two wives are not related to each other.

phrases.english: Two deaf-mute brothers
married to two deaf-mute sisters,
or to two competent sisters,
or to two sisters,
one deaf-mute and one competent.
Or two deaf-mute sisters
married to two competent brothers,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the masculine form in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is the feminine נשואות, since it's talking about the sisters.

phrases.english: or to two deaf-mute brothers,
or to two brothers,
one deaf-mute and one competent —
these are exempt
phrases.notes: The widow is the surviving brother's wife's sister, so she is forbidden to him.

phrases.english: from חליצה and from יבום.
And if they were unrelated women —
they marry them,
phrases.notes: This means the brother does יבום with his brother's widow.

phrases.english: and if they wish to divorce —
they divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי אַחִין חֵרְשִׁין נְשׂוּאִין לִשְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת חֵרְשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the divorce of a חרש / חרשת to יבום cases involving them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the wives are sisters, the widow is exempt from חליצה and יבום. When they are unrelated, the brother does יבום and may later divorce.

steps.title: The deaf brother dies, leaving a competent widow
steps.stepSummary: A deaf brother and a competent brother are married to two competent sisters. The deaf brother dies, and his widow goes free as the surviving brother's wife's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two brothers, one deaf and one competent, are married to two competent sisters. If the deaf one dies, what does the competent brother do? The widow goes free, because she is his wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins the mixed cases. Here the deaf brother dies and the competent brother survives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surviving brother has a full, Torah-level marriage to his own wife. The widow is that wife's sister, so she is forbidden to him. She is released with no יבום and no חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Husband of
She goes free, released without יבום or חליצה

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ,
phrases.english: Two brothers, one deaf-mute and one competent,
married to two competent sisters.
The deaf-mute, husband of the competent one, died.
What should the competent husband of the competent one do?
She goes free because she is his wife's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ, נְשׂוּאִין לִשְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת פִּקְּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the detailed mixed cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deaf brother's widow is released as אחות אשה.

steps.title: The competent brother dies, leaving the deaf brother stuck
steps.stepSummary: Now the competent brother dies. The deaf brother must divorce his own wife, and the widow is forbidden to him forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the competent brother dies, what does the deaf brother do? He divorces his own wife with a גט, and his brother's wife is forbidden to him forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the previous case. Now the deaf brother is the survivor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow's bond to the surviving brother comes from a full Torah marriage, while the deaf brother's own marriage is only rabbinic. So her bond is stronger, and he must divorce his wife. Even then he cannot marry the widow, because she is his ex-wife's sister. He cannot do חליצה either, because a חרש cannot perform it, so she stays forbidden forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Divorces with a bill of divorce
Forbidden forever, with no way out

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a marriage to a חרש is weaker than a full Torah marriage, and that a חרש's inability to do חליצה can leave a woman with no solution.

phrases.english: If the competent husband of the competent one died,
what should the deaf-mute husband of the competent one do?
He divorces his wife with a גט,
and his brother's wife is forbidden forever.
phrases.notes: He can't marry her, since she is his ex-wife's sister, and as a חרש he can't do חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת פִּקֵּחַ בַּעַל הַפִּקַּחַת, מָה יַעֲשֶׂה חֵרֵשׁ בַּעַל פִּקַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses which brother dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deaf brother divorces his wife, and the widow is permanently forbidden to him.

steps.title: Two competent brothers; the deaf wife's husband dies
steps.stepSummary: Two competent brothers are married to one deaf sister and one competent sister. The deaf sister's husband dies, and she goes free as the survivor's wife's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two competent brothers are married to two sisters, one deaf and one competent. If the husband of the deaf one dies, what does the husband of the competent one do? She goes free, because she is his wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new setup. Now the brothers are both competent, and one of the wives is the deaf one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The survivor's own marriage is a full marriage. The deaf widow is his wife's sister, so she is released with no יבום or חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Competent men (plural)

phrases.english: Two competent brothers
married to two sisters,
one deaf-mute and one competent.
If the competent husband of the deaf-mute died,
what should the competent husband of the competent one do?
She goes free because she is his wife's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי אַחִין פִּקְחִין נְשׂוּאִין לִשְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת, אַחַת חֵרֶשֶׁת וְאַחַת פִּקַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New combination: the deafness is now on the wives' side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deaf widow is released as אחות אשה.

steps.title: The competent wife's husband dies: divorce and חליצה
steps.stepSummary: If the competent sister's husband dies, the surviving brother divorces his deaf wife and releases the widow with חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husband of the competent one dies, what does the husband of the deaf one do? He divorces his own wife with a גט, and he releases his brother's wife through חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the previous case. The widow is now the competent sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The competent widow's bond comes from a full marriage, so it is stronger than his rabbinic-level marriage to his deaf wife, and he must divorce the deaf wife. Unlike step 14, both he and the widow are competent, so they can do חליצה and she is not stuck.

keyTerms.meaning: Through חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: A full Torah marriage outranks a marriage involving a חרש or חרשת. Whether the widow ends up stuck or free depends on whether the survivor is able to do חליצה.

phrases.english: If the competent husband of the competent one died,
what should the competent husband of the deaf-mute do?
He divorces his wife with a גט,
and his brother's wife through חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת פִּקֵּחַ בַּעַל פִּקַּחַת, מָה יַעֲשֶׂה פִּקֵּחַ בַּעַל הַחֵרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses step 15. It parallels step 14, but here חליצה is possible.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He divorces his deaf wife and does חליצה with the competent widow.

steps.title: Deaf and competent brothers married to deaf and competent sisters: the deaf brother dies
steps.stepSummary: A deaf brother and a competent brother are married to a deaf sister and a competent sister. The deaf husband of the deaf sister dies. His widow goes free because she is the surviving brother's wife's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two brothers, one deaf and one competent, are married to two sisters, one deaf and one competent. If the deaf brother, husband of the deaf sister, dies, what should the competent brother, husband of the competent sister, do? She goes free because she is his wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets up a new pairing: the deaf brother is married to the deaf sister, and the competent brother is married to the competent sister. It then rules on the first death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surviving brother is fully married to the competent sister, which is a full Torah marriage. The widow's own marriage was only rabbinic, so his tie to her is weak. His real marriage to her sister wins, and she goes free with no יבום and no חליצה as אחות אשה.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute man or woman, treated as lacking full legal understanding
A competent, hearing and speaking man or woman
Wife's sister, a woman forbidden to a man while his wife is alive
She goes out, meaning she is released with no יבום or חליצה

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ,
phrases.english: Two brothers, one deaf-mute and one competent,
are married to two sisters,
one deaf-mute and one competent.
If the deaf-mute brother, husband of the deaf-mute sister, died,
what should the competent brother, husband of the competent sister, do?
She goes free because she is his wife's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ, נְשׂוּאִין לִשְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת, אַחַת חֵרֶשֶׁת וְאַחַת פִּקַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new pairing to the list: this time a deaf brother is married to a deaf sister.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deaf widow goes free as אחות אשה of the competent surviving brother.

steps.title: Same case: the competent brother dies
steps.stepSummary: The competent husband of the competent sister dies. The deaf brother must divorce his deaf wife, and the widow is forbidden to him forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the competent brother, husband of the competent sister, dies, what should the deaf brother, husband of the deaf sister, do? He divorces his wife with a גט, and his brother's wife is forbidden to him forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the case. Now the brother with the full Torah marriage dies, and the deaf brother survives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow was fully married, so the tie of יבום to her is strong. His own marriage to her sister is only rabbinic and is weaker, so he must send his wife away with a גט. Even so, he cannot do יבום with the widow, because she is his ex-wife's sister. He also cannot do חליצה, because he is deaf, so she stays forbidden forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Divorces with a bill of divorce
Forbidden forever, with no way to release her

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 17. There, the stronger marriage belonged to the survivor, so the widow simply left. Here, the stronger marriage belonged to the one who died, so the survivor's own weaker marriage has to give way.

phrases.english: If the competent brother, husband of the competent sister, died,
what should the deaf-mute brother, husband of the deaf-mute sister, do?
He divorces his wife with a bill of divorce,
and his brother's wife is forbidden to him forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת פִּקֵּחַ בַּעַל פִּקַּחַת, מָה יַעֲשֶׂה חֵרֵשׁ בַּעַל חֵרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second possible death in the same case as step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deaf brother divorces his wife, and the widow is forbidden to him forever.

steps.title: Deaf and competent brothers married to unrelated competent women: the deaf brother dies
steps.stepSummary: The wives are now not sisters and both are competent. When the deaf brother dies, the competent brother may choose חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two brothers, one deaf and one competent, are married to two unrelated competent women. If the deaf brother dies, what should the competent brother do? Either he does חליצה or he does יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new set of cases where the wives are unrelated, so the wife's-sister problem disappears. Here the deaf brother dies first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the women are not sisters, nothing blocks יבום. The surviving brother is competent and the widow is competent, so both חליצה and יבום are possible. He may choose either one.

keyTerms.meaning: Unrelated women, meaning the two wives are not sisters
Performs חליצה, the release ceremony
Performs יבום, marrying the brother's widow

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ,
phrases.english: Two brothers, one deaf-mute and one competent,
are married to two unrelated competent women.
If the deaf-mute brother, husband of a competent woman, died,
what should the competent brother, husband of the competent woman, do?
Either he performs חליצה or he performs יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ, נְשׂוּאִין לִשְׁתֵּי נׇכְרִיּוֹת פִּקְּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from sisters to unrelated wives, so the wife's-sister issue no longer applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The competent brother may do either חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: Same case: the competent brother dies, and the deaf brother must marry and never divorce
steps.stepSummary: When the competent brother dies, the deaf brother marries the widow through יבום and can never divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the competent brother dies, what should the deaf brother do? He marries her through יבום, and he never divorces her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other death in the case from step 19. Now the surviving brother is the deaf one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deaf man cannot do חליצה, so יבום is the only way forward. A deaf man's יבום still works, because it is done by the act of living together. That creates a strong marriage, which his weak, rabbinic-level גט cannot undo, so he can never divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes her in, meaning he marries her through יבום
He may never divorce her

phrases.english: If the competent brother, husband of the competent woman, died,
what should the deaf-mute brother, husband of the other competent woman, do?
He marries her and may never divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת פִּקֵּחַ בַּעַל פִּקַּחַת, מָה יַעֲשֶׂה חֵרֵשׁ בַּעַל פִּקַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second possible death in the case from step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The deaf brother does יבום and may never divorce her.

steps.title: Two competent brothers with a competent wife and a deaf wife: the deaf wife's husband dies
steps.stepSummary: Two competent brothers are married to two unrelated women, one competent and one deaf. When the deaf woman's husband dies, the other brother marries her and may later divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two competent brothers are married to two unrelated women, one competent and one deaf. If the husband of the deaf woman dies, what should the husband of the competent woman do? He marries her, and if he wants to divorce her, he may divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new setup. This time both brothers are competent, and one of the wives is deaf. Here the deaf woman is left a widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deaf woman cannot do חליצה, so the only option is יבום. The brother is competent, and her original marriage was only rabbinic. So his גט is able to end this marriage, and he may divorce her afterward if he wants.

keyTerms.meaning: Competent men, meaning both brothers here are competent
If he wants to divorce, he may divorce

steps.confusionAlert: Compare this with step 20. There, the deaf husband could never divorce. Here, the husband is competent, so he can.

phrases.english: Two competent brothers
are married to two unrelated women,
one competent and one deaf-mute.
If the competent brother, husband of the deaf-mute woman, died,
what should the competent brother, husband of the competent woman, do?
He marries her, and if he wants to divorce her, he may divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי אַחִין פִּקְחִין נְשׂוּאִין לִשְׁתֵּי נׇכְרִיּוֹת, אַחַת פִּקַּחַת וְאַחַת חֵרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Swaps which side is deaf: now the brothers are both competent and one wife is deaf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He does יבום with the deaf widow and may divorce her afterward.

steps.title: Same case: the competent wife's husband dies, so it is a normal choice of חליצה or יבום
steps.stepSummary: When the husband of the competent woman dies, the surviving brother (the deaf woman's husband) may do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husband of the competent woman dies, what should the husband of the deaf woman do? Either he does חליצה or he does יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second death in the case from step 21. One more pairing follows in steps 23 and 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow is competent, the surviving brother is competent, and the women are unrelated. So this is a completely regular case of יבום. His own wife being deaf makes no difference to the widow.

keyTerms.meaning: Either ... or, meaning he may choose

steps.whatToRemember: Pattern for the whole series: a חרש or חרשת cannot do חליצה, so when one of them is involved, the only option is יבום. A marriage involving a חרש or חרשת is weaker (rabbinic). A deaf husband's גט cannot end a full יבום marriage, but a competent husband's גט can end a weaker one.

phrases.english: If the competent brother, husband of the competent woman, died,
what should the competent brother, husband of the deaf-mute woman, do?
Either he performs חליצה or he performs יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת פִּקֵּחַ בַּעַל פִּקַּחַת, מָה יַעֲשֶׂה פִּקֵּחַ בַּעַל חֵרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second possible death in the case from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A normal case: he may do either חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: Deaf and competent brothers with unrelated wives: the deaf brother dies
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives its last case. When the deaf brother dies, the competent brother marries the deaf widow and may divorce her later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two brothers, one deaf and one competent, are married to two unrelated women, one deaf and one competent. If the deaf brother (the deaf woman's husband) dies, the competent brother marries her, and if he wants to divorce her, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets up a new case: one brother is deaf and one is competent, and their wives are unrelated (one deaf, one competent). It rules on what happens when the deaf brother dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time one brother is deaf and one is competent, and the deaf woman is married to the deaf brother. When he dies, the competent brother does יבום with the deaf widow. Since the first marriage was only rabbinic, he is allowed to divorce her afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute man / woman, treated as lacking full legal understanding
A competent (hearing and speaking) man / woman
Here: women who are not related to each other
He marries her (does יבום)
He may send her out, meaning divorce her with a גט

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ,
phrases.english: Two brothers, one deaf and one competent,
are married to two unrelated women,
one deaf and one competent.
If the deaf brother, husband of the deaf woman, dies,
what should the competent brother, husband of the competent woman, do?
He marries her,
and if he wants to divorce her, he may divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last variation in the משנה's series. Now one brother is deaf and one is competent, and the wives are unrelated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the deaf brother dies, the competent brother does יבום with the deaf widow and may divorce her afterward.

steps.title: Deaf and competent brothers with unrelated wives: the competent brother dies
steps.stepSummary: When the competent brother dies, the deaf brother marries the competent widow and may never divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the competent brother (the competent woman's husband) dies, the deaf brother marries her and can never divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second half of the same case: the competent brother dies, leaving a competent widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first marriage was a full Torah marriage, so the bond to the deaf brother comes from the Torah. When he takes her, the יבום takes full effect. A divorce from a deaf man is not strong enough to undo it, so he can never divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: He may never divorce her

steps.whatToRemember: This משנה keeps coming back to one idea: a deaf man's own marriage or divorce is only rabbinic. So when the dead brother's marriage was a Torah marriage, the deaf brother can do יבום but can never divorce afterward.

phrases.english: If the competent brother, husband of the competent woman, dies,
what should the deaf brother, husband of the deaf woman, do?
He marries her and may never divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת פִּקֵּחַ בַּעַל פִּקַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the case begun in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the competent brother dies, the deaf brother does יבום with the widow and can never divorce her.

steps.title: Why marriage for a deaf person but not for an imbecile?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks why the רבנן set up marriage for a deaf man and woman, but not for a שוטה and שוטה. He quotes a ברייתא to show that a שוטה's marriage counts for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: Why is a deaf man and woman different, that the רבנן set up marriage for them, while an imbecilic man and woman did not get marriage from the רבנן? As a ברייתא teaches: if a שוטה or a קטן married women and died, their wives are free from חליצה and from יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רמי בר חמא asks why the רבנן treated a חרש and a שוטה differently, since neither has full understanding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumed that a deaf person has a rabbinic marriage. But a ברייתא shows a שוטה has no marriage at all, because his widow needs no חליצה or יבום. Both lack full understanding, so why the difference?

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who asks the question here
What is the difference? (asking why two cases are treated differently)
The רבנן set up (gave) a rabbinic marriage
A mentally incompetent man / woman
Free from both חליצה and יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Even though this is phrased as a question, it is not attacking the משנה. רמי בר חמא accepts both rules and simply wants to know the reason for the difference.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rami bar Ḥama said:
What is different about a deaf man and a deaf woman,
that the Sages set up marriage for them,
and what is different about an imbecilic man and woman,
that the Sages did not set up marriage for them?

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן שֶׁנָּשְׂאוּ נָשִׁים וּמֵתוּ —
phrases.english: As it is taught: an imbecile and a minor who married women and died,

phrases.aramaic: נְשׁוֹתֵיהֶן פְּטוּרוֹת מִן הַחֲלִיצָה וּמִן הַיִּבּוּם!
phrases.english: their wives are exempt from ḥalitza and from levirate marriage!
phrases.notes: If the widow needs neither, it means the marriage never counted at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: מַאי שְׁנָא חֵרֵשׁ וְחֵרֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by asking about the idea behind the משנה, that a deaf person gets a rabbinic marriage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do a deaf man and woman get a rabbinic marriage, while a שוטה and שוטה do not?

steps.title: A marriage with an imbecile cannot last
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן gave marriage to deaf people because such a marriage can work. A marriage with a שוטה cannot last, since no one can live with a snake in one basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a deaf man and woman, where the rabbinic enactment can actually work, the רבנן set up marriage. For an imbecilic man and woman, where the enactment cannot work, because a person cannot live with a snake in one basket, the רבנן did not set up marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רמי בר חמא. A marriage with a deaf person can last, but a marriage with a שוטה cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is whether the marriage will actually work. Deaf people can live together peacefully, so a rabbinic marriage makes sense. A שוטה is impossible to live with, so the רבנן saw no point in enacting a marriage that would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbinic enactment can last (can actually work)
One basket, meaning tight shared living space
A snake

phrases.english: A deaf man and woman, where the Sages' enactment can last,
the Sages set up marriage for them.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹטֶה וְשׁוֹטָה, דְּלָא קָיְימָא תַּקַּנְתָּא דְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: An imbecilic man and woman, where the Sages' enactment cannot last,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין אָדָם דָּר עִם נָחָשׁ בִּכְפִיפָה אַחַת —
phrases.english: since a person does not live with a snake in one basket,
the Sages did not set up marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֵרֵשׁ וְחֵרֶשֶׁת, דְּקָיְימָא תַּקַּנְתָּא דְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's question about the שוטה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן only enacted marriage where it can actually last. A deaf person's marriage can last; a שוטה's cannot.

steps.title: Why marriage for a deaf person but not for a minor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the קטן from the ברייתא. Why did the רבנן give marriage to a חרש but not to a קטן?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is a minor different, that the רבנן did not set up marriage for him, while a deaf man did get marriage from the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second person in the ברייתא, the קטן. It asks why he gets no rabbinic marriage when a deaf man does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The snake answer does not fit a קטן, since living with a child is not dangerous. So the גמרא needs a different reason why a minor gets no rabbinic marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor boy (under בר מצוה age)

phrases.english: And what is different about a minor,
that the Sages did not set up marriage for him,
while for a deaf man the Sages did set up marriage?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא קָטָן דְּלָא תַּקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן נִשּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the שוטה, the גמרא asks about the קטן from the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does a קטן get no rabbinic marriage while a חרש does?

steps.title: A minor will grow up and marry by Torah law; a deaf person will not
steps.stepSummary: A חרש will never be able to marry by Torah law, so the רבנן gave him a rabbinic marriage. A קטן will grow up and marry properly, so there was no need.
steps.simpleTranslation: A deaf man, who will never come to the status of (Torah) marriage, the רבנן set up marriage for. A minor, who will come to the status of marriage, the רבנן did not set up marriage for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is about the future. A קטן will one day be able to marry by Torah law, but a חרש never will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbinic marriage was made for someone who would otherwise never be able to marry. A חרש stays a חרש, so without the רבנן he could never marry. A קטן only has to wait until he grows up, so he does not need a special enactment.

keyTerms.meaning: Will come to the status of (Torah-level) marriage

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן gave a rabbinic marriage only to someone who needs it and can keep it up. That fits the חרש. A שוטה cannot keep a marriage going, and a קטן does not need it because he will grow up and marry by Torah law.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two answers explain why the whole משנה treats a deaf person's marriage as real at the rabbinic level. That is why a deaf person's cases keep needing their own special rules about יבום and divorce.

phrases.english: A deaf man, who will not come to the status of marriage,
phrases.notes: He means marriage by Torah law, which a deaf man can never have.

phrases.english: the Sages set up marriage for;
a minor, who will come to the status of marriage,
the Sages did not set up marriage for.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֵרֵשׁ, דְּלָא אָתֵי לִכְלַל נִשּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the קטן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חרש will never be able to marry by Torah law, so he needed a rabbinic marriage. A קטן will grow up and marry by Torah law, so the רבנן did not enact one for him.

steps.title: A minor girl will grow up, yet she got a rabbinic marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 28: a קטנה will one day marry by Torah law, yet the רבנן still set up a rabbinic marriage for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at a minor girl: she will grow up and be able to marry, and still the רבנן set up a marriage for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave about the קטן. It points to a case that seems to break that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 said the רבנן did not bother with a rabbinic marriage for a קטן, because he will grow up and marry by Torah law. But a קטנה will also grow up, and the רבנן did give her a rabbinic marriage. So the reason from step 28 seems not to hold.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor girl, under the age of adulthood
She will come to be able to marry properly (by Torah law)
The רבנן made an enactment, set up a rabbinic rule

phrases.english: But look at a minor girl,
who will come to be able to marry,
and the רבנן set up marriage for her!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי קְטַנָּה, דְּאָתְיָא לִכְלַל נִשּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 28 with a counterexample.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 28 that the רבנן give a rabbinic marriage only to someone who could never marry by Torah law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קטנה will grow up and marry by Torah law, yet she received a rabbinic marriage. So 'will grow up' does not stop the רבנן from enacting.

steps.title: The minor girl's marriage protects her from being treated as ownerless
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן made a marriage for a קטנה for a different reason: so that people would not treat her as ownerless.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is so that people should not treat her as ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The קטנה's marriage was made for her protection, not because she could never marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without some kind of marriage, a young girl could be treated as if she belonged to no one, and people might take advantage of her. That special danger is a reason of its own. A קטן does not face the same danger, so the rule from step 28 still stands for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Treating something as ownerless, free for anyone to take
There, in that case

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rabbinic enactment can have more than one reason. The קטנה case rests on protecting her, not on the 'can never marry' reason.

phrases.english: There —
phrases.notes: Meaning in the case of the minor girl.

phrases.english: so that people will not treat her
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: as something ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — שֶׁלֹּא יִנְהֲגוּ בָּהּ מִנְהַג הֶפְקֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing reason: the קטנה case has its own separate reason for the enactment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קטנה case seemed to show that the רבנן enact marriage even for someone who will grow up, breaking the rule of step 28.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קטנה's marriage was enacted to protect her from being treated as ownerless. Step 28's reasoning about the קטן still holds.

steps.title: Why can a minor girl refuse, but a deaf woman cannot?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a קטנה can undo her rabbinic marriage through מיאון, while a חרשת, whose marriage is also rabbinic, cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference between a minor girl, who can refuse, and a deaf woman, who cannot refuse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question comparing two rabbinic marriages, the קטנה and the חרשת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both marriages exist only by rabbinic law. A קטנה can leave hers by מיאון, simply declaring she does not want her husband. So why didn't the רבנן give a חרשת the same way out?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
She refuses (does מיאון), undoing a rabbinic marriage by declaring she does not want her husband
A deaf woman (who cannot hear or speak)

phrases.english: And what is different about a minor girl, that she can refuse,
and what is different about a deaf woman,
that she cannot refuse?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא קְטַנָּה דִּמְמָאֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why each marriage was enacted to how each one can end.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the רבנן gave מיאון to a קטנה but not to a חרשת, even though both marriages are rabbinic.

steps.title: The answer begins: if a deaf woman could refuse...
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with 'because if so', which leads into the reason given on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if so...
steps.whatsHappening: These are only the opening words of the answer. The גמרא is setting up the reason, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer works by imagining what would happen if the רבנן had given a חרשת the power of מיאון. The problem that would cause is spelled out right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: Because if so, if that were the rule

phrases.english: Because if so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if the רבנן had let a deaf woman refuse. The rest of the answer comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִם כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the opening of the answer: it will show the bad result that would follow if a חרשת could do מיאון. The full reason continues afterward.
